# Independent audit of the complete two-positive functional envelope

Source: `candidate 31dd328861ee872c`,
Sections 1--6, including the corrected stronger stability threshold H_b.

give products omitting other vertices or resolve OC.

## Attainment and feasible motions

The negative infimum is bounded below by -1. A minimizing sequence has a
subsequence in the closed parameter cube. All its possible boundary
limits are accounted for. When S=sum x_i tends to zero, E lies between
S and S/(1-S), so 1-S/E<=S and each factor 1+x_i/E<=2. Hence L<=2^m S.
The separate h->0 and h bounded below arguments make R->0. When rho->0,
L->1 and R<=1 suffice. The h->1 limit with finite positive E has R->0.
Upper-coordinate faces are covered by the independently proved entropy
boundary theorem, and zero coordinates delete with exact cancellation
of the h powers. Induction on the fixed finite dimension is therefore
legitimate, and a negative infimum is attained in the stated interior.

The unequal-pair motion is a true two-sided variation of T=u+v when
u!=v. Its strict negative second derivative forces equal coordinates.
At equality, the exponential opposite motion increases T to second
order and gives the necessary one-sided derivative condition Delta_T>=0.
It stays within the original open cube and preserves E exactly.

## Stationarity and the corrected stability threshold

I independently differentiated L=(E-mx)(E+x)^m/E^(m+1), using
E'=m(E+1)/(1-x), and obtained the stated logarithmic derivative in (5).
The h-stationarity relation gives F/(1-F)=h(h-x)/D with D>0. Substituting
this into the common-x derivative of R gives the other formula in (5).
All logarithmic quantities and cancellation factors are strictly positive.

The pair-motion derivatives give exactly

    E(h-x)A>=h(E+x)Z.

The corrected difference is

    E(h-x)A-h(E+x)Z
      =x{h(E+1)(E-mx)-EA}.

Thus h>=H_b=EA/[(E+1)(E-mx)], and direct subtraction yields

    H_b-h_c=Z^2/[E(E+1)(E-mx)]>0.

The earlier weaker factorization is not used. Z>0 follows from strict
convexity of E and xE'-E=Z/(1-x). Therefore H_b>h_c>x is sound.

## Critical location and all-dimensional signs

The displayed derivative f'(h) agrees with differentiating
(E+h)^2(h-x)^m/h^(m+1). The substitution y=x/(h-x), r=x/E gives exactly
the cubic product in Section 4 minus r^2(1+y)^(m+2). Its constant and
linear terms cancel, leaving y^2 B. For m>=2, B is strictly concave in y
and tends to minus infinity. At h=1, f'(1)-1=Z/(1-x)>0. These facts prove
one and only one critical point of R, a maximum, on x<h<1.

The lower bound y_c>=1/m follows from the finite geometric series for E.
For the upper bound I independently differentiated the logarithmic
Padé expression; its derivative is exactly

    m(m-1)(m+1)x^2 /
      [(1-x)(2+(m-1)x)(2-(m+1)x)]>0.

Its sign and the direction of the resulting upper bound on E are correct.
Thus y_c lies in the stated rectangle whenever h_c<1.

B is separately concave in r and y there. Its r-quadratic coefficient
is strictly negative, including m=2. At r=0 one has B=my-1>=0.
Evaluation of the cubic product at r=y=1/m gives precisely the first
inequality in (15); evaluation at r=1/m,y=2/(m+1) gives precisely the
second. The elementary e bounds give strict positivity in every integer
m>=2, with no unverified finite-dimensional exceptions. Separate
concavity then proves strict positivity for all 0<r<1/m throughout the
rectangle. Therefore y_c precedes the unique positive zero of B and
h_max<h_c.

The contradiction with actual pair stability proves nonnegativity by
induction. Once nonnegativity is established, any interior equality is
a local minimum and the identical argument applies because L=R>0.
This correctly proves strictness without assuming a strictly negative
value in the final equality argument. The boundary extension uses only
deletion, continuity, and the proved entropy boundary statement.
